II. A DESCRIPTION OF THE MANNER IN WHICH THE HIGHWAY WILL AFFECT THE SECTION 4(f) LAND 
A. The Location and Amount of Land to be Used by the Highway
The improvement will necessitate the use of land from the Woodrow Wilson Woods of the Thorn Creek Division of the Cook County Forest Preserve District for a temporary easement. This small strip of land north of Lincoln Highway and west of Riegle Road is approximately 0.17 Acres.
B. A Detailed Map Discerning the Essential Elements of the Highway Section 4(f) Land Involvement
General maps descerning the area of the Highway/Section 4(f) Land involvement are shown as Exhibit E. A more detailed aerial photograph and drawing of the Forest Preserve Land involvement adjacent to the Lincoln Highway improvement has been included in this report as Exhibit G.
C. The Facilities Affected
Within the Forest Preserve Section 4(f) Land no existing or proposed facilities will be affected by the implementation of this project. There will be some reconstruction of the entrance to the parking facility during construction of Lincoln Highway but access to the park will be maintained.
D. The Probable Increase or Decrease in Physical Effects on the Section 4(f) Land Users
The existing condition of Lincoln Highway between Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road with its deteriorated and narrow pavement is an increasing danger to the motoring public.
The geometric reconstruction, including road widening, channelization, and signalization of major intersections will provide a free flow of traffic that is not expected to change significantly the existing physical impact of noise and air pollution upon Section 4(f) Land users.
There is not anticipated to be any other increase or decrease in the physical effects upon the Section 4(f) Land Users as a result of this proposed improvement. The amount of useable property of the Forest Preserve District, for recreational purposes, will remain unchanged.
